title: Interoception in Adolescents With Restrictive Eating Disorders and Autism Spectrum Disorder
official: "Tuning Into My Body": A Study of Interoception in Adolescents With Restrictive Eating Disorders and Comorbid Autism Spectrum Disorder
summary:
The goal of this observational study is to describe interoception (the ability to sense signals from inside the body, such as heartbeat, hunger, and fullness) in three groups of adolescents aged 13 to 18: those with restrictive eating disorders (REDs), those with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), and those with both REDs and ASD.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* What is the level of interoceptive accuracy (how precisely participants perceive their own heartbeat), as measured by the Heartbeat Counting Task (HCT), in each of the three groups?
* What is the level of interoceptive sensitivity (how participants self-report their awareness of body signals), as measured by the Multidimensional Assessment of Interoceptive Awareness, Version 2 (MAIA-2), in each of the three groups?

In each group, researchers will also explore whether interoceptive accuracy and sensitivity are associated with:

* socio-demographic and clinical characteristics (gender, age, body mass index, illness duration, and IQ)
* psychological characteristics, including alexithymia (difficulty identifying and describing emotions), eating disorder symptoms and their severity, general psychological distress, and emotion dysregulation

Participants will:

* Complete the Heartbeat Counting Task (HCT), in which they silently count their own heartbeats
* Fill in the MAIA-2 questionnaire about body awareness, along with other questionnaires about eating behaviors, emotions, and general well-being

All information will be collected during the standard clinical assessment, with no extra visits or procedures.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Confirmed diagnosis, according to DSM-5-TR criteria, of one of the following: restrictive eating disorder (anorexia nervosa or avoidant/restrictive food intake disorder); autism spectrum disorder, level 1; or restrictive eating disorder with comorbid autism spectrum disorder, level 1
* Age between 13 and 18 years at diagnosis
* Written informed consent freely given and obtained before the start of the study from the participant and/or parent or legal guardian

Exclusion Criteria:

* Intellectual disability (IQ \< 70)
* Insufficient understanding of the Italian language
* Past or current psychotic disorders
